title: Perfect inverse-limit reconstruction over an adically complete ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset A$ an ideal, with $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Given objects $K_n\in D(A/I^n)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and maps $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ in $D(A/I^{n+1})$ inducing isomorphisms $K_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A/I^{n+1}}A/I^n\simeq K_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], suppose $K_1$ is perfect, meaning isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Then $K=R\varprojlim_n K_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit] is perfect and derived $I$-complete in $D(A)$ [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex], and the canonical maps $K\otimes_A^L A/I^n\to K_n$ are isomorphisms compatible with the transitions.

proof.text: Choose a bounded finite-projective representative B of K_1, supported above b. Apply [lem-pc-ring-finite-cone-free-model] to B. Its cone-finiteness hypothesis holds as follows. The cone of a map from a bounded finite-free F to B is bounded above with finite-projective terms. When it is exact above n, descending splitting of the surjections onto cycles, starting above its upper bound, makes its degree-n cycles finite projective. This is the proved library lemma CochainComplex.projective_finite_ker_d_of_exactAt. Its degree-n homology is a quotient of these finite cycles and is therefore finite. The finite-cone free-model theorem gives a bounded-above finite-free complex quasi-isomorphic to B, proving that K_1 is pseudo-coherent by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Tags 09AW and 064U; finite-cone construction, with finite-projective cycles by descending splitting (WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Perfect/FiniteFree.lean)

proof.text: Put $A_n=A/I^n$. Quotient maps $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ are surjective and have square-zero kernel $I^n/I^{n+1}$, since $2n\geq n+1$. Completeness [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] identifies $A$ with their inverse limit. The transition-induced derived reduction isomorphisms are precisely the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-pseudocoherent-inverse-ring-reconstruction], and step 1 supplies its pseudo-coherent first term. Apply it to obtain a bounded-above finite-free limit complex $P^\bullet$ representing $K$, finite-free complexes $P_n^\bullet$ representing $K_n$, and projection-induced chain isomorphisms $q_n:P^\bullet\otimes_A A_n\simeq P_n^\bullet$. In particular $K$ is pseudo-coherent and all its canonical derived reductions are isomorphisms. In Lean, a proved private helper projects this generic reconstruction to the bounded-above finite-free model, its marking, and its first reduction isomorphism before the quotient tower is substituted; no witness is chosen in a public data definition.

source.place: Tags 0CQF, 0CQG and 09AW; apply pseudo-coherent reconstruction to the square-zero quotient tower

proof.text: Every maximal ideal m contains I by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical], so the quotient map A -> A/m factors through A/I. Write P for the bounded-above finite-free model from step 2 and B for the bounded finite-projective model of K_1 from step 1. The complex E obtained by termwise extension of P to A/I represents K_1. Both E and B are bounded above and flat, so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] and [lem-sc-kflat-scalar-extension-derived-iso] identify the homology of their ordinary scalar extensions to A/m. The extension of B has zero terms outside its fixed interval [a,b], so its homology vanishes there. The natural isomorphism for iterated scalar extension identifies the extension of E with the extension of P along A -> A/m. Finally, termwise tensor with the restricted coefficient module A/m is naturally isomorphic to scalar extension followed by restriction; restriction commutes with homology. Since P is bounded above and flat, the proved source-library isomorphism DerivedCategory.QObjTensorSingleFunctorObjIso computes its derived tensor by this termwise tensor complex. Transport through Q(P) ≅ K. This yields a uniform bound [min(a,b),b] for every maximal residue fibre, including the case a>b.

source.place: Tag 0CQG, residue-field argument; Tags 064K, 064L and 06Y0 for the module-complex K-flat comparisons

proof.text: The reconstruction in step 2 makes $K$ pseudo-coherent; the interval in step 3 is independent of the maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pseudocoherent-maximal-fibre-perfect] to $R=A$, $C=K$ and this interval. It gives perfectness of $K$ without imposing any Noetherian, finite-generation-of-$I$, or regularity hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 068V and 0CQG, last sentence of proof

proof.text: After restriction of scalars to $A$, multiplication by $f^n$ is zero on $K_n$ for every $f\in I$: this scalar has zero image in $A/I^n$, and hence acts as the zero endomorphism of every complex representing $K_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-torsion-derived-limit-complete] with $L_n=K_n$ and exponent $e=n$. It proves derived $I$-completeness in the sense of the vanishing definition [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex], not merely an identification with the limit of ordinary reductions.

source.place: Tags 091W and 09AV, completeness argument used by 09AW

proof.text: The composite of the first two arrows in the distinguished Roos triangle is zero. Composing this equality with the nth product projection gives p_n = p_(n+1) followed by the restricted transition: expand the Roos endomorphism as identity minus product shift and use the product projection equations. By the unit formula for the adjunction Hom equivalence, the unit followed by restriction of the adjoint transpose of p_n is exactly p_n. Rewriting both sides of the required consecutive-level compatibility by this equality proves the assertion. No strict-model transition comparison or additional reconstruction property is needed for this step.

source.place: Tag 09AW, final assertion; elementary consequence of the distinguished Roos triangle and the adjunction unit identity
